prerequisites: Students must have passed at least 60 ECTS credits from the basic training module and common industrial branch subjects (first and second year) to enroll in specific technology subjects (third year).

learning_outcomes.text: To know, understand and apply the concepts of science and technology of the different types of hydraulic machines and their corresponding installations.

Apply scientific methodology strategies: analyze the problematic situation qualitatively and quantitatively, propose hypotheses and solutions for the calculation of hydraulic machines and their associated installations.
Adequately communicate knowledge, procedures, results, skills and aspects of hydraulic machines and their installations using specific vocabulary and terminology and appropriate means.
Develop designs and processes for hydraulic installations in accordance with the specific technology of hydraulic machines, applying mandatory specifications and regulations.
Perform measurements, calculations and studies on the operating parameters of different types of hydraulic machines.

syllabus_topics: Hydraulic turbomachinery: generalities and fundamental principles. Definition and classification of hydraulic machines, as well as the fundamental parts of a turbomachine, their forms of representation and velocity triangles. Nomenclature corresponding to heads, flows, powers, losses and efficiencies, both in pumps and turbines. Application of the fundamental theorem of turbomachinery or Euler's theorem to turbines and pumps.

Similarity and dimensional analysis applied to turbomachinery. Analysis of the similarities and analogies that must exist between two turbomachines to transfer their respective behaviors. Determination, using Buckingham's theorem, of the most important dimensionless parameters in turbomachinery, analyzing the fundamental theorem of Combes-Bertrand-Rateau. Introduction to the concept of specific speed and presentation of examples of homologous turbomachines.
Hydraulic turbopumps. Study of the elements, constructive types, characteristic curves, regulation and operation of turbopumps.
Positive displacement machines. Analysis of the different types of positive displacement machines, their elements, their mode of operation and their characteristic curves.
Pumping installations. Study of the calculation and constructive details of simple pumping installations, compound installations, and pressurization installations.
Fans and ventilation installations. Analysis of the elements, constructive types, characteristic curves, regulation and operation of fans, as well as their application to ventilation installations.

Hydroelectric power plants. Description of the general arrangement of hydroelectric power plants. Analysis of the types of heads to consider, the types of hydroelectric power plants, as well as their fundamental constituent elements. Study of the different types of characteristic curves and regulation systems.
Hydraulic turbines. Analysis of the elements, constructive types, characteristic curves, regulation and operation of hydraulic turbines.
Wind power plants. Study of the general theory of wind turbines and Betz's law and description of the different types of wind turbines available.
Water supply and sanitation networks. Study of water abstraction, regulation, conduction and distribution, as well as wastewater collection and distribution.
teaching_methods: Participative resolution of questions and problems

assessment_methods.method: Completion of laboratory practices (exercises, cases or problems)

assessment_rules: For ordinary calls, the final grade is based on a written exam (50%), laboratory practices (20%), and teamwork projects (30%). A minimum score of 4 out of 10 in the written exam is required to combine its result with the continuous assessment components (laboratory + projects); otherwise, the final grade will be the exam score. An alternative final evaluation system is available, requiring individual project submissions before the end of the teaching period. For extraordinary calls, a written exam accounts for 50%, requiring a minimum score of 4 out of 10 to combine with retained positive results from laboratory practices and projects (up to 50%). Negative continuous assessment results from the ordinary call cannot be retained and must be resubmitted, potentially with an oral defense. If no continuous assessment grades exist, a global evaluation through exams and activities is offered, conditioned on submitting projects individually.
